summary: Wilhelm Wundt worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at the universities of Tübingen (~1851-1852), Heidelberg (~1852-1855), and Berlin (~1855-1856), later holding posts at Zurich (1857), Leipzig (1858), and Heidelberg (1864).

Wilhelm von Humboldt was a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied under J. J. Engel, C. K. W. von Dohm, E. F. Klein, G. C. Lichtenberg, C. G. Heyne, and A.-L. Chézy, and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1809-1810).

Will Sweetman is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Cambridge (~1989-1992) and Lancaster University (~1993-1996), and held a post at the University of Otago (~2004).

Willard Gurdon Oxtoby worked in religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Stanford, Princeton, and Harvard, and held academic posts at McGill University (1960-1964), Yale University (1966-1971), and Trinity College/University of Toronto (1971-1999).

Willard Van Orman Quine was a philosopher who studied at Oberlin College (1926-1930) and Harvard University (1930-1931). His career included posts at Harvard (1940-1978), the University of Oxford (~1953-1954), and Wesleyan University (1964-1965).

Willem Bollée was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University (~1947-1956) and the University of Hamburg (~1965-1975). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Münster (1971-1978) and taught at Heidelberg University (~1972-1992).

Willem Caland was an Indologist who completed his doctorate at Leiden University in 1877 under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and Carel Gabriel Cobet. He held positions at Utrecht University (1903, 1906-1929) and Leiden University (1913-1914).

Willem van der Molen is a scholar of linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1970-1983) and subsequently held academic posts at Leiden University (~1978-2017) and the University of Indonesia.
William Blackstone studied at Charterhouse School and Pembroke College, Oxford (~1738-1745). He later held an academic post at the University of Oxford (~1753-1766).

William C. Chittick is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tehran (~1968-1974). He held posts at Sharif University of Technology (~1970-1979), University at Albany, SUNY (~1980-1983), and Stony Brook University (~1983).

William C. Kirby is a historian and sinologist. He studied at Dartmouth and Harvard, the latter under Philip A. Kuhn, and held appointments at Washington University in St. Louis (~1980-1992) and Harvard University (from 1992).
William Carey was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ram Ram Basu and Golok Nath Sharma. In 1801, he took up a post as Professor of Sanskrit and other subjects at Fort William College.

William Dwight Whitney was a linguist and Indologist. He studied under Edward Elbridge Salisbury, Rudolf von Roth, Albrecht Weber, and Karl Richard Lepsius, and was a professor of Sanskrit at Yale University from 1853 to 1894.

William Edelglass is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has held positions at Colby College (attested 2007), Marlboro College (attested 2013), and the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics as a visiting professor.

William Edward Soothill was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of London. He served as president of Shanxi University in 1911 and became Professor of Chinese at Oxford University in 1920.

William Erskine was a scholar in the fields of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He was educated at the Royal High School, Edinburgh, and studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1787-1792).
William Evans Hoyle studied at the University of Manchester and at Christ Church, University of Oxford (~1874-1877).
William F. Powell is a scholar in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He held academic positions at the University of California, Santa Barbara, attested in 1986 and 2026.
William Frederic Sinclair was an Indologist and historian who was educated at the Royal School Dungannon and Armagh. He held a post in the Indian Civil Service beginning in 1866.

William H. Nienhauser, Jr. is a sinologist who studied at Indiana University and Bonn under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff. His appointments include Indiana University (~1972-1973), Kyoto University (~1979-1980), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (from 1983).
